title.en: Order independence, cycle rejection and input typing

summary: Confirm that node values do not depend on evaluation order and that cycles and malformed inputs are rejected at construction.
objective: Two valid topological orders give identical node values, and cycles or malformed inputs produce a rejection rather than a value.
applies_when: A circuit is evaluated with a zero-delay combinational model.
A viewer can connect outputs back to inputs.
Ports, sockets or operator names come from editable data.
intent_signals: the output flickers depending on evaluation order
what happens if I wire the output back
example_prompts: Check that this gate scene rejects feedback connections.

principles: A combinational block is a function of its current inputs, so a result that depends on the order nodes were evaluated in is not combinational.

Cycle rejection is the declared input boundary of a zero-delay evaluator, not a theorem that cycles are unsolvable: a loop can have no consistent assignment, exactly one, or several, and a node whose value is itself combined with a constant false has the unique solution false. The evaluator rejects cycles because it cannot decide among those cases, and it says so.
Type checking is part of the contract: unknown operators, missing drivers and non-Boolean values are rejected rather than coerced.
implementation: Build a fixture with independent parallel branches so that at least two distinct topological orders exist, then evaluate the same input vector in two of them and compare all node values; on a graph whose order is unique, record the check as inapplicable rather than as passed.

Attempt to construct a feedback connection and record the result; the expected outcome is a rejection naming the cycle, stated as an unsupported input rather than as a claim that no assignment exists.
Feed malformed inputs deliberately: an unknown operator name, a missing driver on an input port and a value that is neither true nor false.
Confirm in both directions that every socket drawn in the scene resolves to a declared port on the evaluated graph.
observable_checks: On a fixture admitting two distinct topological orders, both produce identical values at every node; a difference names the node whose value depends on order, and a graph with only one order reports the check as inapplicable.
A feedback connection is rejected with the cycle identified and no output value is produced, and the message describes an unsupported input rather than an unsolvable one.
Malformed inputs are rejected with a message, and no drawn socket lacks a declared port.

known_limits: The cited source presents the functional and timing specification of a combinational device; rejecting cycles is stated here as an implementation requirement of a zero-delay evaluator rather than as a quotation from that source.
Authored verification guidance; no circuit was evaluated or rendered for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: A combinational device is specified by a functional specification such as a truth table or Boolean equations together with a timing specification, and its outputs depend only on its current inputs.
claims.scope: The combinational abstraction as presented in the cited section; that page does not state an explicit acyclicity rule.
